newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Monday November 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Monday November 4.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Former magistrate and Public Works minister Antonio Di Pietro attacks the finance police after leaks in the press concerning alleged irregularities by the Milan magistrates in their corruption probe. "It is a monstrous revenge against (the Milan investigating pool) Clean Hands," he says (all).
* Finance minister Vincenzo Visco defends the finance police, who deny any leak to the press, but says: "It would be very serious should we discover a different version" (all).

* President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro warned against any attempt to divide Italy in a speech apparently directed at secessionist Northern League party leader Umberto Bossi, even if he wasn't specifically mentioned (all).

* Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi in an interview with German newspaper Die Welt am Sonntag said the government is going to apply for the lira to re-enter the ERM in mid-November with a central parity level "slightly above 1.000" per mark. The impact of the Eurotax on families' revenues will be around "0.6-0.7 percent" (Corriere, Repubblica, Stampa).
* The 11.5 trillion lire Eurotax will affect more than 60 percent of taxpayers (Sole 24 Ore).

* In an interview Giorgio Fossa, chairman of Italian employers association Confindustria, says there is no economic recovery and the government is too optimistic over 1997 forecasts: "GDP will not grow more than one percent" (La Stampa).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
